title: Performance and Security Review
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of performance and security review in a jQuery application.
Apply checking script and dependency size in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify auditing unsafe dom insertion with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: Use this lesson on performance and security review as a professional review habit: identify the relevant behavior, make one controlled change, and verify its outcome.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns checking script and dependency size into a repeatable implementation choice. A production review covers version pinning, script integrity where applicable, useful errors, accessible behavior, tested performance, dependency updates, deployment checks, and maintainable documentation.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for performance and security review, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Include performance and security review in a release-readiness checklist. Produce evidence from a repeatable check rather than treating the code example as proof of production readiness.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates performance and security review using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in performance and security review.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: The console lists audit areas to verify with source review, automated tests, and a browser walkthrough; it does not claim the checks are already passed.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Performance and Security Review is one part of the production practices and professional workflows workflow.

A production review covers version pinning, script integrity where applicable, useful errors, accessible behavior, tested performance, dependency updates, deployment checks, and maintainable documentation.
Use the official API or upgrade guide for version-specific behavior and verify an example locally before relying on it.
